useCase.summary: AI assistant that triages a user's inbox and sends replies on the user's behalf

verdict.headline: You can connect Gmail in minutes with Composio managed auth. Production for other users needs Google restricted-scope verification and an annual CASA security assessment, which takes weeks.
verdict.startToday: Start the Google restricted-scope verification and CASA security assessment as soon as the consent screen, privacy policy and demo video exist. Google says this can take several weeks, and nothing else gates launch for external users. Meanwhile, prototype on Composio managed auth.

composio.why: Composio's managed OAuth2 app for Gmail gets you connected immediately for prototyping. For production, a Google Cloud project you own lets you control the consent-screen branding, the privacy policy and the verification and CASA process for your own users. Register Composio's callback URL as the redirect URI on your own client.

neededFor: GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL (only when from_email is not set)

requirements.item: Google Cloud project with the Gmail API enabled and an OAuth client (Web application)
Published branding (Branding page) before requesting data-access verification
Privacy policy on the same domain as the app home page, disclosing how Google user data is accessed, used, stored and shared (Limited Use)
Verified ownership of the authorized domain(s)
Demo video (YouTube, Unlisted) showing the English OAuth consent flow and how each scope is used
CASA security assessment from a Google-empanelled assessor, renewed at least every 12 months

steps.title: Prototype with Composio managed Gmail auth
steps.detail: Create a Composio connection to the gmail toolkit using managed OAUTH2 and test GMAIL_FETCH_EMAILS and GMAIL_SEND_EMAIL with your own Google account.

steps.title: Create Google Cloud project and enable the Gmail API
steps.detail: In the Google Cloud Console create a project, then go to APIs & Services > Library and enable the Gmail API.

steps.title: Publish home page and privacy policy, then verify domain ownership
steps.detail: Host a home page and a privacy policy on the same domain. The policy must describe Google user data use and follow the Limited Use rules. Verify the domain in Google Search Console, for example with a DNS TXT record.

steps.title: Configure Google Auth Platform branding, audience and scopes
steps.detail: Set the app name, logo, home page and privacy policy links, and authorized domains. Set the audience to External. Add only gmail.readonly and gmail.send, plus any Composio-required profile scope. The scopes you request in code must match what is declared here.

steps.title: Create the OAuth client with the Composio callback
steps.detail: Go to Credentials > Create credentials > OAuth client ID > Web application. Add the authorized redirect URI https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add. It must use HTTPS and match exactly. Copy the client ID and secret.

steps.title: Create a Composio auth config with your own client and test
steps.detail: In Composio, create a custom Gmail auth config with your client ID and secret. Add yourself as a test user in Google and run the full triage and reply flow. While the app is in Testing, tokens have a limited lifetime and users are capped.

steps.title: Record the OAuth demo video
steps.detail: Record the English-language consent flow and the features that use gmail.readonly (inbox triage) and gmail.send (replies). Upload it to YouTube as Unlisted.

steps.title: Publish branding and pass Google brand verification
steps.detail: Publish the branding status, then submit for verification in the Verification Center of the Auth Platform. Google reviews branding first.

steps.title: Complete the CASA security assessment
steps.detail: Engage a Google-empanelled CASA assessor, remediate findings and submit the letter of validation to Google. Tier, cost and exact process are not confirmed in our research.

steps.title: Answer reviewer questions and receive restricted-scope approval
steps.detail: Google reviews the data-access request, demo video and assessment result. Respond promptly to reviewer emails. Google says the whole process can take several weeks.

duration.label: 1-7 days (Google: process may take several weeks overall)

steps.title: Move to production and set up recertification
steps.detail: Set the publishing status to In production, confirm that no verification warnings remain, and calendar the 12-month reverification and assessment. Monitor quota usage and back off on 403/429 responses.

risks.title: Restricted scope requires an annual security assessment
risks.symptom: Verification stalls until a CASA letter of validation is provided
risks.fix: Start the assessment early. Budget for the assessor cost, which is not confirmed. Reading mail needs a restricted scope (gmail.readonly), so narrowing scopes cannot avoid it for inbox triage.

risks.title: Unverified app is capped at 100 new users
risks.symptom: Users see the unverified-app screen and sign-ups stop at 100
risks.fix: Limit rollout to test users until verification completes.

risks.title: Testing status limits refresh token lifetime
risks.symptom: Connections need re-authorization after a short period
risks.fix: Expect this during development and publish to production once verified.

risks.title: Scope mismatch between code and consent screen
risks.symptom: Unverified-app screen, or forced re-verification after adding scopes
risks.fix: Declare the final scope set on the consent screen before submitting. Avoid adding scopes later.

risks.title: redirect_uri_mismatch
risks.fix: Register exactly https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add on the OAuth client. Changes can take minutes to hours to propagate.

risks.title: Gmail API quota units
risks.fix: Gmail limits are measured in quota units per project and per user per minute, and new projects get the 2026 quotas. Batch work and use exponential backoff.

claims.text: OAuth client credentials for a server-side Gmail app are created in the Google Cloud Console Credentials page.

sources.title: Using OAuth 2.0 for Web Server Applications | Authorization | Google for Developers
sources.quote: To get these credentials for your application, visit * https://console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials.

verifier.note: The page's code comments say to visit console.cloud.google.com/apis/credentials to get the client ID, secret and redirect URI credentials.

claims.text: Redirect URIs for web server apps must use HTTPS.

sources.title: Manage OAuth Clients - Google Cloud Platform Console Help
sources.quote: Redirect URIs must use the HTTPS scheme, not plain HTTP.

verifier.note: The page says redirect URIs must use HTTPS, but localhost URIs are exempt, so the unqualified claim is too broad.

claims.text: Estimate (not a provider figure): total time to production of roughly 2-14 weeks, dominated by the CASA assessment and Google review. Active developer effort is about 1-4 days.

verifier.note: no source cited

claims.text: Inference: Composio's managed Google app is suited to prototyping. Whether it is verified for gmail.readonly and gmail.send for external users, and what branding users see, was not checked.

verifier.note: no source cited

openQuestions: Is Composio's managed Google OAuth app already verified for gmail.readonly/gmail.send, and can it serve more than 100 external users in production?
What CASA tier, assessor cost and turnaround apply to this app? Google's CASA page was not fetched.
Does the triage feature need gmail.modify (labels, archive)? That is also restricted and would need to be declared before verification.
Does a user-triggered send flow qualify for any lighter review? Reading mail with gmail.readonly still puts the app in the restricted tier.
